questions.q: Two straight paths in a park cross each other. One angle at the crossing is 145°. What is the angle next to it that forms a linear pair with it?
questions.a: 35°, because the two angles of a linear pair add up to 180°, and 180° - 145° = 35°.

questions.q: When two lines intersect at a point on a plane surface, how many angles are formed at that point?
questions.a: 4 angles are formed when two lines intersect.

questions.q: Assertion (A): Two straight lines cross and one of the angles is 72°. The angle vertically opposite it is also 72°. Reason (R): Vertically opposite angles formed by two intersecting lines are always equal.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A: the angle opposite 72° is 72° because vertically opposite angles are always equal.

questions.q: Two straight sticks cross each other, and one of the four angles at the crossing is 64°. Find the other three angles, giving the reason for each.
questions.a: The two angles next to 64° form linear pairs with it, so each is 180° - 64° = 116°. The angle opposite 64° is vertically opposite to it, so it is 64°. The three angles are 116°, 64° and 116°.
s: Finds the two neighbouring angles as 116° using the linear pair (180°)
Finds the opposite angle as 64° using vertically opposite angles

questions.q: True or False: Two straight lines can cross so that one linear pair at the crossing is made of angles of 100° and 90°. Give the reason.
questions.a: False. The two angles of a linear pair always add up to 180°, but 100° + 90° = 190°, so they cannot form a linear pair.
s: States False
Explains that a linear pair adds up to 180° while 100° + 90° = 190°

questions.q: Lines PQ and RS cross at O. Angle POR is 5 times angle ROQ, and these two angles form a linear pair. (a) Write the fact that connects angle POR and angle ROQ. (b) Find both angles. (c) Find angle QOS and angle SOP.
questions.a: (a) Angle POR + angle ROQ = 180°, since they form a linear pair. (b) If angle ROQ = x, then 5x + x = 180°, so 6x = 180° and x = 30°. Angle ROQ = 30° and angle POR = 150°. (c) Angle QOS is vertically opposite angle POR, so it is 150°; angle SOP is vertically opposite angle ROQ, so it is 30°.
s: Part (a): states that the linear pair adds up to 180°
Part (b): finds angle ROQ = 30° and angle POR = 150°
Part (c): finds angle QOS = 150° and angle SOP = 30° using vertically opposite angles

questions.q: Lines AB and CD cross at O. The sum of angle AOC and the angle vertically opposite it, angle BOD, is 3 times angle BOC. (a) Explain why angle BOD = angle AOC and why angle BOC = 180° - angle AOC. (b) Find angle AOC. (c) Write all four angles at O.
questions.a: (a) Angle BOD is vertically opposite angle AOC, so they are equal; angle BOC forms a linear pair with angle AOC, so angle BOC = 180° - angle AOC. (b) Let angle AOC = x. Then x + x = 3(180° - x), so 2x = 540° - 3x, 5x = 540° and x = 108°. (c) Angle AOC = 108°, angle BOC = 72°, angle BOD = 108°, angle AOD = 72°. Check: 108° + 108° = 216° = 3 × 72°.
s: Part (a): gives the vertically opposite and linear pair reasons
Part (b): forms the equation and finds angle AOC = 108°
Part (c): writes the four angles 108°, 72°, 108°, 72°

questions.q: Two straight roads cross at a chowk in Guntur. The four angles at the crossing are named a, b, c and d in order going round the chowk, and angle a = 55°. (a) What do the two angles of a linear pair add up to? (b) Find angle b. (c) Find angle c, which is vertically opposite angle a. (d) Find angle d. (e) Add the four angles and write the total.
questions.a: (a) 180°. (b) Angle b forms a linear pair with angle a, so b = 180° - 55° = 125°. (c) Angle c is vertically opposite angle a, so c = 55°. (d) Angle d is vertically opposite angle b, so d = 125°. (e) 55° + 125° + 55° + 125° = 360°.
s: Part (a): states 180°
Part (b): finds b = 125°
Part (c): finds c = 55°
Part (d): finds d = 125°
Part (e): adds to get 360°

questions.q: Vijayawada's planners must choose one of two road crossings for a petrol pump. At each crossing two straight roads cross. At crossing X, one angle is 36° more than the angle next to it, which forms a linear pair with it. At crossing Y, two vertically opposite angles add up to 160°. The pump needs a corner of at least 100°, a park goes in the corner vertically opposite the pump, and bus stops go in the other two corners, each of which must be at least 75°. (a) Find all four angles at crossing X. (b) Find all four angles at crossing Y. (c) At which crossing(s) can the pump and the park both get a corner of at least 100°? Explain. (d) Which crossing should be chosen? Give the reason.
questions.a: (a) If the smaller angle is x, then x + (x + 36°) = 180°, so 2x = 144° and x = 72°; going round, the angles are 72°, 108°, 72°, 108°. (b) Vertically opposite angles are equal, so each is 160° ÷ 2 = 80°; their neighbours form linear pairs, so each is 180° - 80° = 100°; the angles are 80°, 100°, 80°, 100°. (c) Both. The pump takes the 108° corner at X or the 100° corner at Y, and the corner vertically opposite it is equal, so the park also gets 108° or 100°. (d) Crossing Y. The bus-stop corners are 80° at Y, which is at least 75°, but only 72° at X, which is less than 75°.
s: Part (a): uses the linear pair to find 72°, 108°, 72°, 108°
Part (b): uses vertically opposite angles and the linear pair to find 80°, 100°, 80°, 100°
Part (c): says both, since the park's corner equals the pump's vertically opposite corner
Part (d): chooses Y because its other corners are 80° (at least 75°) while X's are 72°

questions.q: In a geometry figure, how is it shown that two lines are perpendicular to each other?
o: A small square is drawn in the angle between them
A single arrow mark is drawn on each line
Two arrow marks are drawn on each line
A dot is drawn where the lines cross
questions.a: A small square is drawn in the angle between perpendicular lines; arrow marks are used for parallel lines.

questions.q: Rahul draws two straight lines that cross so that all four angles at the crossing are equal. What is the measure of each angle?
questions.a: 90°, because the four equal angles together make 360°, and each neighbouring pair adds up to 180°, so each angle is a right angle.

questions.q: (a) What are perpendicular lines? (b) Give one example of perpendicular lines from your classroom.
questions.a: (a) Perpendicular lines are a pair of lines that intersect each other at right angles (90°). (b) For example, the bottom edge and a side edge of the blackboard, which meet at a corner at 90°.
s: Part (a): states that perpendicular lines meet at 90°
Part (b): gives a correct classroom example

questions.q: True or False: Two lines that cross each other at an angle of 89° are perpendicular. Give the reason.
questions.a: False. Perpendicular lines meet at exactly 90°. Lines crossing at 89° make angles of 89° and 91°, so they are not perpendicular.
s: States False
Explains that perpendicular lines need exactly 90° (the angles here are 89° and 91°)

questions.q: Lines PQ and RS cross at O. Angle POR is (5y + 15)° and the angle next to it, angle ROQ, is (3y + 5)°. (a) Find y. (b) Find angle POR and angle ROQ. (c) Are PQ and RS perpendicular? Give the reason.
questions.a: (a) The two angles form a linear pair, so (5y + 15) + (3y + 5) = 180, giving 8y + 20 = 180, 8y = 160 and y = 20. (b) Angle POR = 5 × 20 + 15 = 115° and angle ROQ = 3 × 20 + 5 = 65°. (c) No. Perpendicular lines meet at 90°, but here the angles are 115° and 65°.
s: Part (a): uses the linear pair to find y = 20
Part (b): finds 115° and 65°
Part (c): decides not perpendicular because the angles are not 90°

questions.q: Two lines cross, and the four angles at the crossing, in order going round, are a, b, c and d. It is known that a + c = b + d. (a) Which of these angles are equal to each other, and why? (b) Use the given fact to show that a = b. (c) Show that the two lines are perpendicular.
questions.a: (a) a = c and b = d, because they are pairs of vertically opposite angles. (b) Since a + c = b + d, we get a + a = b + b, so 2a = 2b and a = b. (c) a and b form a linear pair, so a + b = 180°. With a = b this gives 2a = 180°, so a = 90°. All four angles are 90°, so the lines are perpendicular.
s: Part (a): states a = c and b = d as vertically opposite angles
Part (b): shows a = b from a + c = b + d
Part (c): uses the linear pair to get 90° and concludes the lines are perpendicular

questions.q: A tiler in Bhopal lays square tiles on a floor. The straight grout lines form a grid of three horizontal lines h1, h2 and h3 and two vertical lines v1 and v2. All five lines run across the whole floor, and each horizontal line meets each vertical line at a right angle. (a) What angle does h1 make with v1, and what are such lines called? (b) Is h1 perpendicular to h2? Give the reason. (c) How many pairs of perpendicular lines are there in the grid? (d) How many right angles are formed in all at the crossings of the grid?
questions.a: (a) 90°; such lines are called perpendicular lines. (b) No. h1 and h2 run across the whole floor without ever meeting, so they are parallel; perpendicular lines must intersect each other at 90°. (c) Each of the 3 horizontal lines is perpendicular to each of the 2 vertical lines, so there are 3 × 2 = 6 pairs. (d) There are 6 crossings, each with 4 right angles, so 6 × 4 = 24 right angles.
s: Part (a): states 90° and names them perpendicular
Part (b): says no, because h1 and h2 never meet, while perpendicular lines must intersect at 90°
Part (c): finds 6 pairs
Part (d): finds 24 right angles

questions.q: Which of the following describes parallel lines?
o: A pair of lines on the same plane that do not meet however far they are extended
A pair of lines that meet at exactly one point
A pair of lines that meet at a right angle
Any two lines that do not meet inside the page
questions.a: Parallel lines are a pair of lines on the same plane that do not meet however far we extend them at both ends.

questions.q: Match each mark in a figure in Column I with what it shows in Column II. Column I: 1. A single arrow mark on two lines, 2. A small square in the angle between two lines, 3. Two arrow marks on two other lines, 4. Two lines drawn meeting at a point. Column II: A. The lines are perpendicular, B. A second set of parallel lines, C. A first set of parallel lines, D. The lines intersect.
questions.a: 1-C, 2-A, 3-B, 4-D: one arrow marks the first set of parallel lines, the small square marks perpendicular lines, two arrows mark a second set of parallel lines, and lines that meet at a point intersect.

questions.q: Consider the following statements. Statement I: The opposite edges of a square sheet of paper are parallel to each other. Statement II: Parallel lines lie on the same plane and do not meet, however far they are extended at both ends. Statement III: Once a square sheet has been folded along one diagonal and opened, no other fold can make a crease parallel to that diagonal. Which of the statements are correct?
o: Statements I and II only
Statement I only
Statements II and III only
Statements I, II and III
questions.a: Statements I and II only. Statement III is wrong: a crease parallel to the diagonal can be made, for example by folding one of the two corners that are not on the diagonal onto the centre of the sheet.

questions.q: Anil draws a line l. Using his set square, he draws two lines p and q, each perpendicular to l. (a) What angle does each of p and q make with l? (b) Are p and q parallel? Give the reason.
questions.a: (a) Each makes 90° with l. (b) Yes. Taking l as a transversal, the corresponding angles at p and q are both 90°, so they are equal and p is parallel to q.
s: Part (a): states 90°
Part (b): says parallel because the corresponding angles on l are equal

questions.q: (a) Give two examples of parallel lines on things in your school bag. (b) Lines x and y are drawn on the same page and cross each other when they are extended. Are they parallel? Why? (c) Write the two conditions that two lines must meet to be called parallel.
questions.a: (a) For example, the ruled lines of a notebook page, and the two long edges of a ruler. (b) No. Parallel lines never meet however far they are extended, but x and y meet. (c) They must lie on the same plane, and they must not meet however far they are extended at both ends.
s: Part (a): gives two correct examples
Part (b): says not parallel because the lines meet
Part (c): states same plane and never meet however far extended

questions.q: Mira wants to draw a line through point A that is parallel to a line l, using a ruler and a set square. Which method works?
o: Place one edge of the set square along l, hold a ruler firmly against another edge, slide the set square along the ruler until the first edge reaches A, and draw along that same edge
Place one edge of the set square along l, slide the set square freely across the page without any ruler until that edge reaches A, and draw along that edge
Place one edge of the set square along l, hold a ruler firmly against another edge, slide the set square along the ruler until A is reached, and draw along a different edge
Place a ruler along l, set the set square against the ruler so that one edge is at right angles to it and passes through A, and draw along that edge
questions.a: Sliding the set square along a fixed ruler keeps its edge at the same angle to the ruler, so the corresponding angles stay equal and the new line through A is parallel to l.

questions.q: Assertion (A): A square sheet is folded in the middle to make a vertical centre crease, and then its left and right edges are folded onto the centre crease. The two new creases are parallel to the centre crease. Reason (R): Each new crease lies halfway between an edge and the centre crease all the way from top to bottom, so it stays the same distance from the centre crease and never meets it.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A: lines on the same sheet that stay the same distance apart never meet, so they are parallel.

questions.q: Pooja draws two lines l and q on a sheet. A transversal t gives corresponding angles of 70° at l and 74° at q. She says: 't was a bad choice. If I draw a different transversal, I may get equal corresponding angles, and then l and q will turn out to be parallel.' (a) Using t, are l and q parallel? Give the reason. (b) Is Pooja right that another transversal could give equal corresponding angles? Explain. (c) What will happen if l and q are extended far enough?
questions.a: (a) No. The corresponding angles are 70° and 74°, which are not equal, but for parallel lines the corresponding angles are always equal. (b) No. When two lines are not parallel, the corresponding angles formed by any transversal can never be equal, so no other transversal can help. (c) l and q lie on the same sheet and are not parallel, so they will meet (intersect) at some point.
s: Part (a): says not parallel because 70° and 74° are unequal
Part (b): says no transversal can give equal corresponding angles for lines that are not parallel
Part (c): says the lines will meet

questions.q: A line t crosses two other lines l and m at two different points. How many angles are formed in all?
questions.a: 8 angles are formed: 4 at the crossing with l and 4 at the crossing with m.

questions.q: A transversal t crosses line l at P and line m at Q. Nobody knows whether l and m are parallel. Only the upper-right angle at P is measured: it is 70°. How many of the other seven angles can be found from this one reading?
questions.a: 3: the other three angles at P follow from linear pairs and vertically opposite angles (110°, 70°, 110°). No angle at Q can be found, because l and m are not known to be parallel.

questions.q: A transversal t crosses line l at P and line m at Q, with l above m. At P the angles are angle 1 (above l, left of t), angle 2 (above l, right of t), angle 3 (below l, right of t) and angle 4 (below l, left of t); at Q, angles 5, 6, 7 and 8 are in the same positions around Q. (a) Which four of the eight angles lie between the lines l and m? (b) Which angle at Q is in the same position as angle 2, and what is such a pair called?
questions.a: (a) Angles 3, 4, 5 and 6: angles 3 and 4 are below l, and angles 5 and 6 are above m. (b) Angle 6; angle 2 and angle 6 are corresponding angles.
s: Part (a): names angles 3, 4, 5 and 6
Part (b): names angle 6 and calls the pair corresponding angles

questions.q: A transversal crosses two lines l and m. At the crossing with l, one of the angles is 75°. At the crossing with m, one of the angles is 95°. (a) Write the measures of all four angles at l. (b) Write the measures of all four angles at m. (c) How many different measures appear among the eight angles, and can l and m be parallel?
questions.a: (a) 75°, 105°, 75°, 105° (linear pairs add to 180°, vertically opposite angles are equal). (b) 95°, 85°, 95°, 85°. (c) Four different measures: 75°, 105°, 95° and 85°. The lines cannot be parallel, because then each angle at m would equal its corresponding angle at l, and the angles at m would be only 75° and 105°.
s: Part (c): counts four measures and explains that the lines are not parallel

questions.q: A transversal t crosses line l at P and line m at Q, with l above m. At P, the angle above l and left of t is (2x + 10)° and the angle above l and right of t is (x + 20)°. At Q, the angle above m and left of t is 2y° and the angle below m and right of t is (y + 52)°. (a) Find x. (b) Write all four angles at P. (c) Find y. (d) Write all four angles at Q. (e) How many different measures appear among the eight angles, and are l and m parallel? Give the reason.
questions.a: (a) The two angles at P form a linear pair: (2x + 10) + (x + 20) = 180, so 3x + 30 = 180 and x = 50. (b) 110°, 70°, 110°, 70° (above-left 110°, above-right 70°, below-right 110°, below-left 70°). (c) The two angles at Q are vertically opposite, so 2y = y + 52 and y = 52. (d) Above-left 104°, above-right 76°, below-right 104°, below-left 76°. (e) Four different measures: 110°, 70°, 104°, 76°. The lines are not parallel, because the corresponding angles above-left at P (110°) and above-left at Q (104°) are not equal.
s: Part (a): uses the linear pair to find x = 50
Part (b): writes 110°, 70°, 110°, 70° at P
Part (c): uses vertically opposite angles to find y = 52
Part (d): writes 104°, 76°, 104°, 76° at Q
Part (e): counts four measures and decides not parallel since corresponding angles differ

questions.q: Assertion (A): When a transversal crosses two lines, four pairs of vertically opposite angles are formed. Reason (R): At each of the two crossing points, the four angles form two pairs of vertically opposite angles.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A: two crossing points with two pairs each give four pairs.

questions.q: A straight village road t crosses two straight canals l and m near Karimnagar. The engineer names the angles at the crossing with l as angle 1 (above l, left of t), angle 2 (above l, right of t), angle 3 (below l, right of t) and angle 4 (below l, left of t). At m he names them angles 5, 6, 7 and 8 in the same positions. He measures angle 1 = 125° and angle 5 = 125°. (a) Find angle 2. (b) Find angle 3. (c) Which angle at m is the corresponding angle of angle 2? (d) Are the canals parallel? Give the reason.
questions.a: (a) Angle 2 forms a linear pair with angle 1, so it is 180° - 125° = 55°. (b) Angle 3 is vertically opposite angle 1, so it is 125°. (c) Angle 6. (d) Yes. Angles 1 and 5 are corresponding angles and both are 125°, so the canals are parallel.
s: Part (a): finds angle 2 = 55°
Part (b): finds angle 3 = 125°
Part (c): names angle 6
Part (d): says parallel because corresponding angles 1 and 5 are equal

questions.q: A transversal crosses line l and then line m. At l the angles are angle 1 (above l, left), angle 2 (above l, right), angle 3 (below l, right) and angle 4 (below l, left); at m, angles 5, 6, 7 and 8 are in the same positions. Which angle is the corresponding angle of angle 3?
o: Angle 7
Angle 5
Angle 6
Angle 8
questions.a: Angle 7, because it is in the same position at m (below the line, right of the transversal) as angle 3 is at l.

questions.q: Two parallel lines are crossed by a transversal. One angle at the first line is 58°. What is its corresponding angle at the second line?
questions.a: 58°, because corresponding angles formed by a transversal on parallel lines are always equal.

questions.q: A transversal crosses two lines l and m. A pair of corresponding angles at l and m measure 74° and 74°. (a) Are l and m parallel? (b) Give the reason.
questions.a: (a) Yes, l and m are parallel. (b) When the corresponding angles formed by a transversal on a pair of lines are equal, the lines are parallel.
s: Part (a): says the lines are parallel
Part (b): gives the reason that the corresponding angles are equal

questions.q: True or False: When a transversal crosses two parallel lines, every pair of corresponding angles is equal. Give the reason.
questions.a: True. Corresponding angles formed by a transversal intersecting a pair of parallel lines are always equal; tracing one angle and placing it on its corresponding angle shows they match.
s: States True
Gives the fact that corresponding angles on parallel lines are always equal

questions.q: A transversal t crosses line l and line m, with l above m. At l, the angle above l and right of t is 108°. At m, the angle below m and right of t is 72°. (a) Find the angle above m and right of t. (b) Name the angle at l that corresponds to it. (c) Are l and m parallel? Give the reason.
questions.a: (a) The angle above m and right of t forms a linear pair with the 72° angle, so it is 180° - 72° = 108°. (b) The angle above l and right of t, which is 108°. (c) Yes. These corresponding angles are both 108°, so l and m are parallel.
s: Part (a): finds 108° using the linear pair
Part (b): names the angle above l and right of t as the corresponding angle
Part (c): concludes parallel because the corresponding angles are equal

questions.q: A railway inspector checks three straight rails l, m and n, which should all be parallel. A straight rod t is laid across all three, with l at the top, then m, then n. At l, the angle above l and right of t is 76°. At m, the angle below m and left of t is 76°. At n, the angle below n and right of t is 106°. (a) Find the angle above m and right of t, and give the reason. (b) Find the angle above n and right of t, and give the reason. (c) Which rails are parallel to l? (d) Which rail must be realigned, and what should its angle above the rail and right of t become?
questions.a: (a) 76°, because it is vertically opposite the angle below m and left of t. (b) 180° - 106° = 74°, because it forms a linear pair with the angle below n and right of t. (c) Only m. The angle above m and right of t corresponds to the 76° angle at l and is equal to it, so m is parallel to l; the corresponding angle at n is 74°, not 76°, so n is not parallel to l. (d) Rail n must be realigned so that its angle above n and right of t becomes 76°, equal to the corresponding angle at l.
s: Part (a): finds 76° as vertically opposite
Part (b): finds 74° from the linear pair
Part (c): compares corresponding angles and says only m is parallel to l
Part (d): chooses n and gives 76° as the needed corresponding angle

questions.q: Dhruv draws a line l and a transversal t crossing l at X, so that the angle above l and right of t is 50°. He marks a point Y on t above X and wants to draw a line m through Y parallel to l. (a) What angle should m make with t above m and right of t, and what is this pair of angles called? (b) Explain why m will then be parallel to l. (c) Find the angle below l and right of t at X. (d) After m is drawn, find the angle below m and left of t at Y. (e) His friend draws a line through Y making 130° above the line and right of t. Will that line be parallel to l? Explain.
questions.a: (a) 50°; the 50° angle at X and this angle at Y are corresponding angles. (b) If the corresponding angles formed by t on l and m are equal, the lines are parallel. (c) It forms a linear pair with 50°, so it is 180° - 50° = 130°. (d) It is vertically opposite the 50° angle above m and right of t, so it is 50°. (e) No. The corresponding angles would be 50° at X and 130° at Y, which are not equal, so that line is not parallel to l.
s: Part (a): states 50° and names corresponding angles
Part (b): explains that equal corresponding angles make the lines parallel
Part (c): finds 130° using the linear pair
Part (d): finds 50° using vertically opposite angles
Part (e): decides not parallel because 130° is not equal to 50°

questions.q: The white stripes of a zebra crossing are parallel, and a cyclist's straight track crosses two of them. Between the two stripes, the angle at the upper stripe on the right of the track is 64°. What is the angle between the stripes at the lower stripe on the left of the track?
questions.a: 64°, because the two angles lie between the parallel stripes on opposite sides of the track, so they are alternate angles, and alternate angles on parallel lines are equal.

questions.q: A transversal crosses line l and then line m. At l the angles are angle 1 (above l, left), angle 2 (above l, right), angle 3 (below l, right) and angle 4 (below l, left); at m, angles 5, 6, 7 and 8 are in the same positions. Match each pair in Column I with its name in Column II. Column I: 1. Angle 1 and angle 5, 2. Angle 1 and angle 3, 3. Angle 1 and angle 2, 4. Angle 3 and angle 5. Column II: A. Alternate angles, B. Linear pair, C. Corresponding angles, D. Vertically opposite angles.
questions.a: 1-C, 2-D, 3-B, 4-A: angles 1 and 5 are in the same position (corresponding), 1 and 3 are opposite at one crossing (vertically opposite), 1 and 2 are neighbours on a line (linear pair), and 3 and 5 lie between the lines on opposite sides of the transversal (alternate).

questions.q: Assertion (A): Alternate angles formed by a transversal crossing two parallel lines are equal. Reason (R): Alternate angles lie on the same side of the transversal.
o: A is true, but R is false
Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is false, but R is true
questions.a: A is true, but R is false: alternate angles are equal on parallel lines, but they lie on opposite sides of the transversal, not the same side.

questions.q: A transversal crosses parallel lines l and m, with l above m. At l the angles are angle 1 (above l, left), angle 2 (above l, right), angle 3 (below l, right) and angle 4 (below l, left); at m, angles 5, 6, 7 and 8 are in the same positions. (a) Name the alternate angle of angle 4. (b) If angle 4 = 65°, find its alternate angle.
questions.a: (a) Angle 6 (above m, right of the transversal). (b) Alternate angles on parallel lines are equal, so angle 6 = 65°.
s: Part (a): names angle 6
Part (b): finds 65° because alternate angles are equal

questions.q: The capital letter N is painted on a signboard. Its two upright strokes are parallel, and a slanting stroke joins the top of the left upright to the bottom of the right upright. At the top joint, the angle between the left upright and the slanting stroke is 28°. (a) Which angle at the bottom joint is the alternate angle of this 28° angle? (b) What is its measure? (c) Which fact about the two uprights did you use?
questions.a: (a) The angle between the right upright and the slanting stroke at the bottom joint. (b) 28°. (c) The two uprights are parallel, and alternate angles formed by a transversal (the slanting stroke) on parallel lines are equal.
s: Part (a): names the angle between the right upright and the slanting stroke
Part (b): states 28°
Part (c): uses that the uprights are parallel so alternate angles are equal

questions.q: Parallel lines l and m, with l above m, are crossed by three transversals t, s and r. For each transversal, the angle below l on its right and the angle above m on its left are measured. For t they are (3k - 10)° and (2k + 15)°; for s they are (4j - 30)° and (j + 54)°; for r they are (5p - 35)° and (3p + 5)°. (a) Find k and the angle for t. (b) Find j and p, and the angles for s and r. (c) Which two of the transversals are parallel to each other? Give the reason.
questions.a: (a) The two angles are alternate angles on parallel lines, so they are equal: 3k - 10 = 2k + 15, which gives k = 25, and the angle is 65°. (b) 4j - 30 = j + 54 gives 3j = 84, so j = 28 and the angle for s is 82°; 5p - 35 = 3p + 5 gives 2p = 40, so p = 20 and the angle for r is 65°. (c) t and r. Taking l as a transversal of t, s and r, the angles below l on the right of each are corresponding angles: 65°, 82° and 65°. Those of t and r are equal, so t is parallel to r; s makes 82°, so it is parallel to neither.
s: Part (a): finds k = 25 and 65°
Part (b): finds j = 28 with 82° and p = 20 with 65°
Part (c): picks t and r using equal corresponding angles on l, and rules out s

questions.q: Parallel lines l and m are crossed by a transversal t, with l above m. The angle below l and left of t is (x + 25)°, and its alternate angle, above m and right of t, is (2x - 15)°. What is the angle above l and left of t?
questions.a: 115°: the alternate angles are equal, so x + 25 = 2x - 15 and x = 40, making the angle below l and left of t 65°; the angle above it forms a linear pair with it, so it is 180° - 65° = 115°.

questions.q: Two parallel lines are crossed by a transversal. One of the interior angles on the left of the transversal is 72°. What is the other interior angle on the left of the transversal?
questions.a: 108°, because interior angles on the same side of a transversal crossing parallel lines add up to 180°, and 180° - 72° = 108°.

questions.q: Two parallel lines are crossed by a transversal. Consider the following statements. Statement I: The interior angles on the same side of the transversal add up to 180°. Statement II: If the transversal is perpendicular to one of the lines, it is perpendicular to the other line too. Statement III: The interior angles on the same side of the transversal are always equal. Which of the statements are correct?
o: Statements I and II only
Statement I only
Statements II and III only
Statements I, II and III
questions.a: Statements I and II only. Statement II holds because the corresponding angle at the other line is also 90°. Statement III is wrong: the two interior angles add up to 180°, so they are equal only when both are 90°.

questions.q: Assertion (A): The two interior angles on the same side of a transversal crossing two parallel lines can both be acute angles. Reason (R): The interior angles on the same side of a transversal crossing two parallel lines add up to 180°.
o: A is false, but R is true
Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
questions.a: A is false, but R is true: two acute angles add up to less than 180°, so they cannot be the two interior angles on the same side, which always add up to 180°.

questions.q: True or False: Two parallel lines are crossed by a transversal. If one interior angle is 64°, the interior angle on the same side of the transversal at the other line is 116°. Give the reason.
questions.a: True. Interior angles on the same side of a transversal crossing parallel lines add up to 180°, and 64° + 116° = 180°.
s: States True
Uses the 180° sum of interior angles on the same side: 64° + 116° = 180°

questions.q: Two parallel handrails l (upper) and m (lower) of a staircase are joined by a straight slanting support t. On the left of t, the interior angle at l is 3 times the interior angle at m. (a) Write an equation for the two interior angles. (b) Find both angles. (c) Find the angle above l and left of t.
questions.a: (a) If the interior angle at m is x, then x + 3x = 180°, since interior angles on the same side add up to 180°. (b) 4x = 180°, so x = 45°; the angles are 45° at m and 135° at l. (c) The angle above l and left of t forms a linear pair with the 135° interior angle, so it is 180° - 135° = 45°.
s: Part (a): writes x + 3x = 180°
Part (b): finds 45° and 135°
Part (c): finds 45° using the linear pair

questions.q: A carpenter checks three wall racks A, B and C. Each rack has an upper shelf l and a lower shelf m, crossed by one straight slanting support t. On each rack he measures the angle below l on the left of t, and one angle at m. Rack A: 64° at l, and the angle below m on the right of t is 116°. Rack B: 72° at l, and the angle below m on the left of t is 108°. Rack C: 55° at l, and the angle above m on the right of t is 57°. (a) For each rack, find the angle above m on the left of t. (b) For each rack, find the sum of the two interior angles on the left of t. (c) Which rack has parallel shelves? Give the reason. (d) His helper says Rack B is fine because 72° + 108° = 180°. Explain the helper's mistake. (e) Keeping 55° at l on Rack C, what should the angle above m on the right of t read if the shelves were parallel?
questions.a: (a) Rack A: 116°, vertically opposite the 116° angle. Rack B: 180° - 108° = 72° (linear pair). Rack C: 180° - 57° = 123° (linear pair). (b) Rack A: 64° + 116° = 180°. Rack B: 72° + 72° = 144°. Rack C: 55° + 123° = 178°. (c) Only Rack A. On parallel shelves the interior angles on the same side of the support add up to 180°; Racks B and C fail this. For Rack A, the angle below m on the left of t is 180° - 116° = 64°, equal to its corresponding angle 64° at l, so its shelves are parallel. (d) The 108° angle is below m, outside the shelves, so it is not an interior angle; the interior angle at m is 72°, and 72° + 72° = 144°, not 180°. (e) The interior angle at m should be 180° - 55° = 125°, so the angle above m on the right of t should be 180° - 125° = 55°.
s: Part (a): finds 116°, 72° and 123°
Part (b): finds the sums 180°, 144° and 178°
Part (c): picks Rack A with the reason
Part (d): explains that 108° is outside the shelves, not an interior angle
Part (e): finds 55°

questions.q: A carpenter in Anantapur has made two trapezium-shaped frames, X and Y, for the front of a shop counter. In each frame ABCD, the top bar AB must be parallel to the bottom bar DC, with A above D on the left and B above C on the right; AD and BC are slanting side bars. He measures the inside corner angles. Frame X: angle A = 112°, angle D = 68°, angle B = 97°, angle C = 83°. Frame Y: angle A = 110°, angle D = 74°, angle B = 106°, angle C = 70°. (a) Taking AD as a transversal of AB and DC, what kind of angle pair are angle A and angle D? (b) For Frame X, find angle A + angle D and angle B + angle C. (c) For Frame Y, find the same two sums. (d) In which frame is AB parallel to DC? Give the reason.
questions.a: (a) They are interior angles on the same side of the transversal AD. (b) 112° + 68° = 180° and 97° + 83° = 180°. (c) 110° + 74° = 184° and 106° + 70° = 176°. (d) Frame X. If AB were parallel to DC in Frame Y, these interior angles would add up to 180°, but they add up to 184° and 176°, so Y's bars are not parallel. In Frame X, the angle between DC and AD extended below D is 180° - 68° = 112°, equal to its corresponding angle A = 112°, so AB is parallel to DC.
s: Part (a): names interior angles on the same side of the transversal
Part (b): finds 180° and 180°
Part (c): finds 184° and 176°
Part (d): picks Frame X with the reason

questions.q: Two straight parallel roads l and m are crossed by two straight parallel streets p and q, making four crossings: A (l and p), B (l and q), C (m and p) and D (m and q). At crossing A, the angle above the road and right of the street is 65°. (a) Find the angle in the same position at B. (b) Find the angle in the same position at C. (c) Find the angle in the same position at D. (d) How many different angle measures appear among all 16 angles at the four crossings? Name them.
questions.a: (a) 65°: with road l as the transversal of the parallel streets p and q, these are corresponding angles. (b) 65°: with street p as the transversal of the parallel roads l and m, these are corresponding angles. (c) 65°: with street q as the transversal of l and m, it corresponds to the 65° angle at B. (d) Two measures: 65° and 115°, because at each crossing the other angles are 180° - 65° = 115° (linear pair) or 65° (vertically opposite).
s: Part (a): finds 65° at B using corresponding angles
Part (b): finds 65° at C using corresponding angles
Part (c): finds 65° at D
Part (d): states two measures, 65° and 115°

questions.q: How are two adjacent edges of a square sheet of paper related to each other?
o: They are perpendicular
They are parallel
They never meet
They meet at an angle of 45°
questions.a: They are perpendicular: adjacent edges meet at a point and form right angles.

questions.q: A square sheet is folded horizontally in half and opened. Why is the new crease parallel to the top edge?
o: Both make a right angle with the vertical edges, so the corresponding angles are equal
Both are made by folding the same sheet
Both meet the vertical edges at 45°
The crease is longer than the top edge
questions.a: Both the crease and the top edge make 90° with a vertical edge, which acts as a transversal, so the corresponding angles are equal and the lines are parallel.

questions.q: A square sheet of paper is folded vertically in half, then folded vertically in half again, and opened. (a) How many parallel vertical lines can be seen now, counting the left and right edges? (b) What angle do these lines make with the top edge?
questions.a: (a) 5 lines: the two edges and three creases (the first fold makes 1 crease and the second fold makes 2 more). (b) 90°; the vertical lines are perpendicular to the top edge.
s: Part (a): counts 5 parallel lines
Part (b): states 90°

questions.q: True or False: On a poster, two long straight lines e and f are drawn over a pattern of circles, and they seem to tilt away from each other. Ravi draws a transversal and measures a pair of alternate angles between e and f exactly: both are 58°. So e and f are not parallel. Give the reason.
questions.a: False. Each 58° alternate angle is vertically opposite an angle that is the corresponding angle of the other, so the corresponding angles are both 58°. Equal corresponding angles mean e and f are parallel; the tilt is only an illusion.
s: States False
Explains that equal alternate angles give equal corresponding angles, so the lines are parallel whatever they look like

questions.q: A square sheet is folded horizontally in half, again and again, and opened after each fold. Lines are counted with the top and bottom edges included. One fold gives 3 lines. Kavya says the number of lines doubles with every fold, so after 7 folds there will be 3 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 = 192 lines. (a) Find the real number of lines after 7 folds. (b) Explain Kavya's mistake. (c) How many new lines does the 7th fold add?
questions.a: (a) Each fold puts a new crease in the middle of every gap, so the gaps double: 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128. Lines = gaps + 1, so after 7 folds there are 128 + 1 = 129 lines (2^7 + 1). (b) It is the gaps between the lines that double, not the lines; for example, after 2 folds there are 5 lines, not 6. (c) After 6 folds there are 64 gaps (65 lines), so the 7th fold adds 64 lines.
s: Part (a): finds 129 lines
Part (b): explains that the gaps double, not the lines, with an example
Part (c): finds 64 new lines

questions.q: In a craft class at a school in Warangal, the children make paper chains. Sana has a square sheet of side 72 cm. She folds it horizontally in half 3 times, opening it after each fold, and then cuts along every horizontal crease to get equal strips. Her friend Ravi has an identical sheet, but he folds it horizontally in half only 2 times before cutting along the creases. (a) How many parallel horizontal lines, edges included, does Sana's sheet show before cutting? (b) How many strips does Sana get, and how wide is each? (c) How many strips does Ravi get, and how wide is each? (d) How many of Sana's strips, laid side by side, are as wide as one of Ravi's strips? Explain using the folds.
questions.a: (a) 2^3 + 1 = 9 lines. (b) The 9 lines leave 8 strips, each 72 ÷ 8 = 9 cm wide. (c) 2^2 + 1 = 5 lines leave 4 strips, each 72 ÷ 4 = 18 cm wide. (d) 2 strips, since 18 ÷ 9 = 2: Sana's third fold puts a crease in the middle of each of Ravi's strips, halving it.
s: Part (a): finds 9 lines
Part (b): finds 8 strips of 9 cm
Part (c): finds 4 strips of 18 cm
Part (d): finds 2 and explains that the extra fold halves each strip

questions.q: Assertion (A): After one horizontal fold in half, a square sheet shows 3 parallel horizontal lines, including its top and bottom edges. Reason (R): Folding the sheet horizontally in half makes a crease midway between the top and bottom edges, parallel to them.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A: the new crease joins the two edges to make 3 parallel lines.
